newsitem.title: USA: U.S. power output falls 1.2 pct vs. year ago - EEI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. power output falls 1.2 pct vs. year ago - EEI.

text.p: Electricity deliveries in the continental U.S. totaled 56,950 gigawatt hours (GWh) for the week ended March 29, down 1.2 percent from the same period in 1996, the Edison Electric Institute (EEI) said Wednesday.
The amount of weekly power supplied to the Pacific Northwest area showed the largest year-to-year decrease, down 8.6 percent to 3,073 GWh, EEI said.
The Pacific Southwest region experienced the largest increase in power output, rising 5.8 percent from the corresponding period a year earlier to 4,542 GWh.
Year-to-date domestic power production for the first 13 weeks of 1997 totaled 815,047 GWh, up 0.1 percent from the same period in 1996, EEI said.
